inputs.text: Tens of thousands were marched through central London on Saturday in a rally coordinated by hundreds of groups. They’ll call it opposition to the far right, but the timing tells a different story: six months after a major far-right demonstration and just weeks before key local elections. This looks less like a spontaneous protest than a coordinated show of force by institutions and campaign networks, designed to steer the political climate before voters get their say. The public message is the cover; the timing is the tell.
